"Terminal value uses distributable equity cash: next normalized owner PAT minus book capital needed for mature growth, divided by cost of equity less terminal growth. The terminal ROE is earned by the modeled earnings and retained book, not assigned a large-broker premium. Dividends leave both cash and book. No historic restricted cash, client balances, AUM or warrant proceeds are added twice. A negative continuing-franchise cash value is floored at zero as a diagnostic, not as an assertion that liquidating financial assets recovers zero. A separate haircut-based asset check is required to interpret the bear case. [E24]"

"The 2017 SEBI order is an important exculpatory finding: the investigated transfers were not established to be prohibited client-fund use, and the proceedings were disposed of without penalty. The June 2022 adjudication is different. It upheld specified client-fund-use violations, including credit-client funds meeting proprietary obligations on admitted dates, but did not proceed with one collateral allegation because of calculation ambiguity. The large aggregate allegation in the show-cause discussion is not an established investor loss and is not used here. The order noted no quantifiable gain/loss or investor complaints and imposed ₹4.5 lakh, subsequently paid. [E09, E10]"
"The 2017 proceedings were dismissed; the 2022 order did not quantify gain/loss or investor complaints. [E09, E10]"

"The annual models link retained fees, funded-credit balances, yields, deposit income, finance costs, overhead, credit losses, capex, new loans/receivables, debt and own-margin needs to distributable cash. Opening available owner cash is assumed zero solely to avoid distributing unverified deposits; actual unrestricted cash is ND. Base and bull assume all remaining warrants convert in year one, adding ₹29.3625 crore cash and 1.7 million shares; the already received ₹9.7875 crore deposit is reclassified to equity without another cash inflow. Bear assumes lapse, no new warrant cash and no new warrant shares. New debt ceilings and rescue share issues are explicitly uncommitted assumptions, never deemed available facilities. "The calculated scenarios are intentionally not ordinary investment forecasts. The base’s low earned terminal ROE makes its continuing-franchise value much lower than a simple earnings multiple; a 12-times terminal earnings cross-check or credible release of excess capital would materially change the outcome. The report therefore shows both the restrictive terminal mechanism and the assumptions needed to improve it, without elevating either to a fair-value recommendation. The bull’s faster credit growth can require fresh equity even while profits rise. Downside is not solved by putting a higher multiple on earnings financed by repeatedly issuing shares. [E24]"

"The canonical factors are GOV 3, MOAT 4, REV 7, DUR 5, CAP 4, CASH NS, BAL 5, EXEC 4, EARN 4, R NS, D 3, P NS and L NS. The higher growth score describes retained operating income, including interest, not a claim of brokerage market-share gains. Each factor has separate supportive and adverse evidence. CASH is NS because an owner-cash and loss-recognition conclusion cannot be extracted from client-inclusive CFO. R and P are NS because diagnostic assumptions are not a defensible investment forecast; L is NS because official turnover/restrictions are incomplete. [E04–E08, E20–E24]"

"The classification is Avoid — governance under the framework’s explicit GOV ≤3 override. GOV 3 is a bounded stewardship assessment: a 2022 SEBI order established historical credit-client money being used for proprietary or other clients’ obligations, and a later inspection disclosed separate client-settlement/reporting failures. This is not a finding of present misuse, quantified investor loss, fraud, insolvency, or suspension of this issuer. The 2017 dismissal of earlier charges, paid penalties, absence of quantified gain/loss in the 2022 order, unmodified financial audit, and historical liquidity evidence are meaningful contrary evidence. [E09–E13]"

Fees depend on funded, active customers and trading frequency, not registered accounts alone. [E04]"

FY22/FY23 property gains recorded inside revenue and FY25 property gains in other income are separately identified. "The linked bear path is falling active-client turnover, lower fees and funding spreads, losses on financed or unsecured accounts, and simultaneous exchange-margin demands. Clients withdraw or become inactive, a few productive authorized persons leave, and receivables cannot be sold at book value. Some borrowings remain payable before collateral can be realized. Higher funding costs and technology/compliance expenses then depress profit further. Client funds cannot lawfully plug the hole. If warrant holders decline to exercise after a price fall, expected equity cash disappears just when it is most needed. [E07–E11, E15–E18, E21]"

"The linked reverse holds credit growth at 10% and sends fee growth through the same annual margin, funding, whole-share issuance, 2% issuance-cost and dividend equations. The 15% investor hurdle is reached only near 94% annual retained-fee growth in the tested 0%–100% range, a highly demanding and rescue-dependent mathematical case, not an operating forecast. A static mature-ROE reverse is also retained but clearly separated. The haircut-based asset check gives roughly ₹50–85 per current share, or ₹66–98 after all conversions, subject to intact post-March receipts and all stated claims/cost assumptions. These values are neither available cash nor guaranteed liquidation recovery. [E24]"

"The model tests a 30% initial retained-fee decline, credit yield compression, 5% annual credit-loss cash charge and a ₹25 crore first-year margin shock. The no-rescue version has a real modeled cash gap; the recapitalized version raises uncommitted equity at ₹75 and dilutes existing holders. Neither establishes that lenders or shareholders would actually subscribe, or that these are the most likely outcomes. A zero continuing-franchise terminal value in this harsh case is not a liquidation appraisal; the balance-sheet haircut check supplies a separate recovery range with legal, timing and client-segregation caveats. The conditional outcomes cannot be probability-weighted into a supported expected return. [E24]"

"The no-rescue branch suppresses IRR and terminal valuation after the first negative-cash breach. Later rows are labeled counterfactual. In lapse branches, warrant deposits remain outside common equity; no forfeiture timing or tax treatment is assumed. "The plausible moat mechanism is relationship-based service, local trust, authorized-person distribution and customer switching inconvenience. It is not exchange exclusivity, patented technology or a demonstrated network effect. ICRA reported 10,782 NSE active clients at March 2025, presence in three cities directly and fifteen through authorized persons, and roughly 34% of H1 FY26 gross brokerage from the ten largest sub-brokers. The latter is concentration in distribution, not ten end customers. Pricing and customer ownership can therefore sit partly with intermediaries rather than PESB. Retained brokerage’s long-run growth is far less impressive than group profit growth. [E04, E08]"

"The sector growth measure is declared before scoring: recurring retained operating income equals net brokerage plus depository fees, net transaction fees, commissions, other customer charges and merchant fees, plus debtor/advance/deposit interest, less finance cost. Proprietary trading, investment/share gains, property gains and miscellaneous nonrecurring other income are excluded. This is a financial-intermediary net-income measure before staff and overhead, not industrial gross sales, AUM growth or a claim that all deposits belong to shareholders. The same definition is used in all six years. Historical classification and rounding limitations are recorded, rather than selecting a flattering three-year window. [E03–E05]"

It is a qualitative comparator here, not a fabricated like-for-like valuation multiple. [E23]"
